about.intro_content: Prof. Xiao-Shi Zhang is Professor and Vice Director of the Tumor Biotherapy Department at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou, specialising in comprehensive treatment of melanoma and immunotherapy for liver, colon, lung, breast and other cancers.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Zhang has been a key investigator in landmark anti-PD-1 immunotherapy trials for Chinese melanoma patients, including the pivotal POLARIS-01 phase II trial of toripalimab as salvage monotherapy in advanced melanoma, published in Clinical Cancer Research, with five-year follow-up results confirming durable benefit. He has also contributed to trials combining toripalimab with novel agents such as HBM4003 (an anti-CTLA-4 antibody) and thymosin α1 for elderly patients with advanced melanoma. He completed a visiting scholarship at Karolinska University, Sweden.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Xiao-Shi Zhang

items.question: Does Prof. Xiao-Shi Zhang accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to melanoma immunotherapy at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Zhang's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Zhang specialises in comprehensive immunotherapy treatment of melanoma, and also provides immunotherapy for liver, colon, lung and breast cancer.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is Prof. Zhang involved in landmark melanoma trials?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Zhang was a key investigator in the POLARIS-01 phase II trial of toripalimab in advanced melanoma, the largest prospective anti-PD-1 study in a population where acral and mucosal melanoma predominate.

items.question: Does Prof. Zhang offer treatment options for elderly melanoma patients?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Zhang has researched combination regimens such as thymosin α1 plus toripalimab specifically designed with elderly patients' immune profile and comorbidities in mind.
